manifest.name: dsh-codex-style-worktree
manifest.description: Codex 风格 Worktree：新建会话时在工作区旁选择「本地」或「新建本地工作树」，发送首条消息后自动创建独立检出并在输入框上方显示进度，侧边栏标记托管会话；清理有保护、删除前留可恢复快照，所有配置都能在设置页在线修改。
manifest.author: wplct

scripts.verify: npm test && npm run smoke && node --check client/client.js

bundle.text:
# dsh-codex-style-worktree bundle patch: inserts the plugin row into the profile roster.
# Plain `insert` row only (id + name, no config, no expressions) so dshmarket can
# hot-mount it without a restart; every knob has a default in lib/config.js and
# can be overridden from the profile's own cordis.patch.yml like any other row.
- insert:
    - id: codex-worktree
      name: dsh-codex-style-worktree

readme.text:
**English** | [简体中文](README.zh.md)

> A "work like Codex" placement choice for DSH sessions: on the new-session hero row, pick **Local** or **New local worktree** (the default) next to the workspace chip; after you send the first message the plugin creates a detached checkout and switches **that session's** cwd into it. No new Workspace, no naming, no branch from the plugin (Git owns branch naming at commit time).

- Version: `0.5.1` (2026-10-20; package / plugin id / loader row name: `dsh-codex-style-worktree`; profile-patch insert row id: `codex-worktree`)
- API namespace: `/api/dsh-codex-style-worktree`, RPC method prefix `dsh-codex-style-worktree/`; sidecar: `$DSH_HOME/dsh-codex-style-worktree/state.json`; disable marker: `.dsh-codex-style-worktree-off`
- GitHub: <https://github.com/wplct/dsh-codex-style-worktree>
- Requirements: DSH `0.2.0-rc.2` / `0.2.1-rc.2`, Node.js `>= 22.19.0`, `git` on PATH
- License: MIT

readme.section: 0.5.1: the checkout is created on the first message
readme.text:
- **Bug fixed**: opening a blank Session no longer creates a checkout. The desktop fires `agent/created` the moment the New Session appears — long before the first prompt — so the old wiring decided the work location at Session-open time; a choice made in that blank Session therefore applied only to the *next* Session (switching to Local still created a checkout, switching back to New local worktree created none).
- Creation now runs on the first step of the Session's first turn (`agent/pre-step` with `turn === 1`) — i.e. after you send the first message — and the per-workspace placement is read at that moment, so the choice made in the blank Session applies to **that** Session.
- Blank Sessions no longer leave stray checkouts behind; the progress card and sidebar marker appear after the first message instead of when the blank Session opens.
- Nothing else changes; there is no config, sidecar or settings migration. Upgrade with `dsh plugin --profile desktop update dsh-codex-style-worktree` and reopen DSH once.

- Package name / plugin id / loader row name / API namespace / RPC prefix / sidecar directory all move from `dsh-codex-worktree` to `dsh-codex-style-worktree`; the display title "Codex-style Worktree" is unchanged.
- The **settings namespace stays `codex-worktree`** (the profile-patch insert row id is untouched), so saved settings survive; every editable field is unchanged.
- On first boot the sidecar directory migrates automatically from `~/.dsh/dsh-codex-worktree` to `~/.dsh/dsh-codex-style-worktree` (rename, no data loss; if the rename fails the old directory keeps being read).
- The repository opt-out marker is now `.dsh-codex-style-worktree-off`; the old `.dsh-codex-worktree-off` is still honored.
- Upgrade path: remove the old package, install the new one (`dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-codex-worktree`, then `dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:wplct/dsh-codex-style-worktree`), then fully quit and reopen DSH once.

| Capability | 0.3.0 | 0.4.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cleanup guard | Cleanup deletes directly | Refused when the checkout is **another** active session's current cwd (`worktree-in-use`); cleaning your own session's checkout first moves its cwd back to the workspace; `force` overrides after confirmation |
| Snapshot before delete | Only autoPrune kept a ref for detached commits | Every delete path: when the checkout is detached and `HEAD ≠ baseCommit`, write `refs/dsh-codex-style-worktree/<timestamp+session suffix>` and record it in the sidecar |
| Snapshot restore | Manual `git branch` only | `/wt-snapshots`, `/wt-restore <ref>`, and a "recoverable snapshots" list in the settings page |
| Archive cleanup | Checkouts always kept after a session ends | Optional `cleanupOnArchive` (default off): a lazy sweep removes clean, unused checkouts after archive |
| RPC | 6 endpoints | 7 (adds `restore`); the `list` response gains per-repository `snapshots` |
| Sidecar | v2 | v3 (adds a `snapshots` map; v1/v2 are migrated in memory on read, no data loss) |

| Capability | 0.2.x | 0.3.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| When the worktree is created | Automatically for every new session (no choice); a "New Worktree" button could also create one on demand | You choose a placement on the hero row; the worktree is created **after the first message** (first-turn `agent/pre-step`) |
| Selector location | A dock button above the composer | The hero workspace row: a pill between `📁 workspace ▼` and `standard mode ▼` |
| Remembered choice | None | **Per workspace**, persisted in the sidecar (`placements`), restart-safe |
| Workspace | The old button called `workspaces.create`, cluttering the sidebar | **Never creates a Workspace**; only the session cwd changes |
| Progress feedback | None | Inline three-step progress card above the composer (projection-driven, minimum 1 s) |
| Sidebar | No marker | Managed sessions show a **read-only** worktree icon (tooltip = checkout path) |
| Settings page | Read-only config | **Editable form**; save writes the active profile patch and applies live (volatile, no restart) |
| State sync | Some RPC reads | Everything is event/projection-driven, **zero polling** |
| RPC | Included `create`, etc. | `status/list/clean/prun

Position: the official **`conversation.hero.options`** seat — the compact options area of the New Session row, right-aligned after the workspace and preset controls, rendered only once the blank new Session exists. It sits on the same row as `📁 workspace ▼` and `standard mode ▼`:

- Options (single select, current one ticked):
  - `Local` / `本地` — run directly in the current workspace directory;
  - `New local worktree` / `新建本地工作树` — run in a new checkout (**default**);
  - Grey hint at the bottom of the menu: `Creating a local worktree does not add a Workspace; it only switches this Session’s working directory.`
- Visibility: only on the **blank new-session hero row** (this seat is session-scoped, so it renders once the blank Session exists); hidden for non-Git workspaces (`isGit=false` from the host) and for existing sessions.
- Seat choice: this is the official list seat, **not** the shipped WorkspacePicker's `conversation.hero.workspace` (that seat is `kind: "single"` and owned by the workspace picker; registering there would shadow the shipped workspace switcher). The plugin registers under its own id in `conversation.hero.options` and **never shadows** shipped UI.
- Persistence: the choice is written back immediately through the `placement` RPC and stored per workspace path in the sidecar. The control updates optimistically and rolls back with a message if the write fails; if reading fails it degrades to a read-only display of the default and never blo

```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ⑂ Creating worktree                                │
│   ✓ Prepare workspace                              │
│   ◐ Check out files                                │

- The card is shown for **at least 1000 ms** (creation is usually < 0.5 s); on completion all three steps are ticked and `Worktree created` fades out after ~400 ms.
- **Only "Cancel" is offered**: it hides the card immediately while creation continues; the plugin does **not** roll back and offers no "don't use a worktree" remedy.
- Failure: the card turns into an error state with the reason, and the session continues in its **original directory** without blocking the conversation. Error codes:

| Error code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `not-git-repository` | The workspace is not a Git repository |
| `no-commit` | The repository has no commit yet |
| `disabled` | `enabled: false`, or `.dsh-codex-style-worktree-off` exists at the repository root |
| `root-unreachable` | The configured `root` is not writable, or the session sandbox forbids that path |
| `limit-reached` | The repository reached `maxPerRepo` (clean up old checkouts first) |
| other message | git error / timeout etc., shown verbatim |

- The session **always stays with its original Workspace**; the only side effect is `workingDirectory.set` for the current session.
- The plugin never calls `workspaces.create` / `workspaces.rename` / `sessions.create` and never adds a Workspace; acceptance: the number of workspaces in `workspace.json` is unchanged before and after.
- Default `mode: detached`: the plugin **creates no branch**, the checkout stays on a detached HEAD; Git decides the branch name at commit/push time (use `git switch -c` when you want a named branch). `mode: branch` switches to creating `<branchPrefix><name>` up front.

- Slot: `sidebar.session.row.leading` (the official ambient-marker seat: a persistent leading icon area of the session row; the component reads `sessionId`). This is a **deliberate design decision**: the row's action strip is a hover-only button strip and is unsuitable for a permanent marker; the seat does not belong to the shipped workspace picker and never shadows shipped UI.
- Managed sessions show a 14 px worktree icon (`⑂`-style SVG, `currentColor`, muted), with the tooltip `Codex-style Worktree · <checkout path>`.
- **Not clickable**: clicks fall through to the row (keeping "open session"); no hover card and no navigation.
- Data source: the host registers the `codexWorktree` session projection; the client reads `sessions.list.getSnapshot().byId[sessionId].projectionValues?.codexWorktree` and renders the icon only when `phase === 'ready'`, hiding it for `null`/missing. **Zero RPC, zero polling.**
- Creation, cleanup and pruning changes appear immediately via projection pushes.

> Known limitation: when you clean a **non-live session's** checkout from the settings page, the host cannot append a projection event for that session, so its sidebar marker disappears only on that session's next consistency repair (reopening the session or its first step).

- Shows `Codex-style Worktree` plus status (managed / not managed / error).
- Popover: path, repository, base commit, mode, change count (dirty), cleanup action.
- The basic state comes from the projection first; **when you open the popover** it makes one `status` call for details such as the dirty count (on demand, not polling).
- No naming, and no "don't use a worktree" rollback.

Prerequisites: DSH `0.2.0-rc.2` / `0.2.1-rc.2`, Node.js `>= 22.19.0`, `git`; finish or stop running tasks/sessions first.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:wplct/dsh-codex-style-worktree
```

Then **quit and reopen DSH once** (the bundle layer takes effect; this is not a page refresh). Afterwards **configuration changes need no restart** (volatile, live).

**0.5.0 → 0.5.1 (current)**:

- bug fix only: the checkout is created on the first message instead of when a blank Session opens, so the placement choice applies to the Session it was made in;
- no migration: run `dsh plugin --profile desktop update dsh-codex-style-worktree`, then quit and reopen DSH once.

**0.4.x → 0.5.0 (rename-only)**:

The repository also ships a direct-install script that bypasses the package manager, for local development or offline use:

```sh
node install.mjs --dry-run   # print the plan only, write nothing
node install.mjs             # install into the default profile (desktop)
node install.mjs --profile web
DSH_HOME=/path/to/.dsh node install.mjs --profile desktop

What the script does:
The direct installer explicitly does **not**: modify the profile's `package.json`, run `pnpm`/`npm`, or restart DSH.

Uninstall with the symmetric DSH plugin command, then restart DSH:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-codex-style-worktree
```

If the package was installed with the **direct-install** script from section 3.3, use `uninstall.mjs` instead:

```sh
node uninstall.mjs --dry-run   # print the plan only
node uninstall.mjs             # default profile
node uninstall.mjs --profile web
```

`uninstall.mjs` removes the marked block (markers and everything between them, other lines preserved, file backed up to `.bak-<ISO timestamp>` first) from `<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`, deletes `<profile>/node_modules/dsh-codex-style-worktree/` recursively, and prints every action and backup path; it is idempotent and `--dry-run` writes nothing. It also reports (without deleting) install snapshots `.dsh-codex-style-worktree.previous-*` and the sidecar ledger.

| Goal | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Full uninstall | `dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-codex-style-worktree` (direct install: `node uninstall.mjs`), then restart DSH |
| Revert the profile patch only | `cp <profile>/cordis.patch.yml.bak-<timestamp> <profile>/cordis.patch.yml`, delete `node_modules/dsh-codex-style-worktree/` manually, restart |
| Roll back to the previous package | rename the printed `.dsh-codex-style-worktree.previous-<timestamp>` directory back to `node_modules/dsh-codex-style-worktree`, restart |

Uninstall never deletes your worktrees or branches: check `/wt-status`, clean up with `/wt-clean`, or run `git worktree remove <path>` / `git branch -d <branch>` yourself. Deleting the sidecar ledger (`$DSH_HOME/dsh-codex-style-worktree/`) also clears the remembered placements.

| Field | Type | Default | Control | Constraints / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | switch | Master switch; when off, new sessions get no worktree (existing checkouts are untouched) |
| `defaultPlacement` | `worktree`\|`local` | `worktree` | select | Placement for a workspace with no stored record yet |
| `directory` | string | `.agents/worktrees` | text | Pool directory: relative, no `.`/`..` segments |
| `root` | string | `""` | text | Empty = inside the repository; may be absolute or repository-relative, no `..` |
| `mode` | `detached`\|`branch` | `detached` | select | `detached` creates no branch (default); `branch` creates `<branchPrefix><name>` up front |
| `namePrefix` | string | `wt-` | text | Checkout name prefix; no `/` `\`, must not start with `-` |
| `branchPrefix` | string | `wt/` | text | Branch prefix for `mode: branch`; must not start with `-` or `/` |
| `baseRef` | string | `HEAD` | text | Local base revision; must not start with `-`; resolved locally (network only via `fetchBeforeCreate`) |
| `fetchBeforeCreate` | boolean | `false` | switch | Run `git fetch --prune origin` before creation; failures only warn and never block;

Hidden internals (not in the form):

| Field | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gitCommand` | `git` | Internal: git executable name/path |
| `cleanupOnDispose` | `false` | Reserved: delete the checkout on session dispose (currently always kept) |
The DSH `workspace-write` file sandbox is bounded by **the session's original workspace directory (`header.cwd`)**, not the whole disk.

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/wt-status` | Show this session's checkout: path, repo, branch (`detached` when detached), base, dirty |
| `/wt-clean [--force] [--branch]` | Remove this session's checkout; refuses uncommitted work or an in-use checkout unless `--force`; `--branch` also deletes the branch (meaningful with `mode: branch`) |
| `/wt-snapshots` | List the **current session's repository** snapshots (all repositories when unmanaged): ref, commit, created time, restored marker |
| `/wt-restore <ref>` | Restore a snapshot into a new detached checkout (`wt-restored-…`) and print the restored path and commit |

readme.section: 6.1 Cleanup entry points and the in-use guard
readme.text:
Three entry points with identical rules:

| Entry point | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `/wt-clean [--force] [--branch]` | Terminal-style management command for this session's checkout |
| Session-header chip popover | Cleans the current session's checkout in place; dirty or in-use checkouts show a confirmation / force affordance |
| Settings page "worktree management" row delete | Cleans any managed checkout from the per-repository list |

readme.section: 6.1 Cleanup entry points and the in-use guard
readme.text:
- **In-use guard (`worktree-in-use`)**: if the checkout directory is the current working directory of **another live session**, deletion is refused with `code=worktree-in-use`. This mirrors Codex, which refuses to delete the "current checkout" outright.
- **Cleaning your own checkout is not refused**: when `/wt-clean` or the current session's chip cleans that session's own checkout, the plugin first moves the session's cwd back to its original workspace (the response carries `movedTo`) and then deletes — the session keeps working.
- **Force override**: after confirming, `force` (the `--force` flag, or the "force clean/delete" button in the UI) overrides the guard — the **other** live sessions lose their working directory (their cwd points at a deleted checkout) and uncommitted changes in the checkout are lost too.
- Dirty checkouts are still refused first with `worktree-dirty`; `force` overrides both the in-use and the dirty check.
- If the snapshot conditions in 6.2 apply, the plugin writes the snapshot ref first and then deletes.

- **When a snapshot is taken automatically**: before deleting a **detached (no branch) checkout whose `HEAD ≠ baseCommit`**, the plugin writes the current `HEAD` as the snapshot ref `refs/dsh-codex-style-worktree/<timestamp+session suffix>` and records it in the sidecar `snapshots`. This applies to every delete path (`/wt-clean`, chip cleanup, settings-page delete, `prune`, the archive lazy sweep).
- `/wt-snapshots`: lists the **current session's repository** snapshots (all repositories when the session is unmanaged): ref, commit, created time, restored marker.
- `/wt-restore <ref>`: restores a snapshot into a **new detached checkout** (named `wt-restored-<timestamp>`) and returns `{ ref, path, commit, repoRoot }`; the restored checkout is **not bound to the original session** and **does not switch any session's cwd** — it just brings the data back.
- **Settings page "worktree management"**: the `list` response carries a **top-level** `snapshots` array (each row has `repoRoot`, newest first) and the page groups it by repository into a "recoverable snapshots" list (ref, commit, created, restored marker); clicking *Restore* creates a new checkout and refreshes the list.
- A restored

- Setting `cleanupOnArchive` (boolean, default `false`): after a session is **archived**, delete its **clean** worktree.
- It is a **non-polling lazy sweep** that runs opportunistically when: a new session is created successfully, the worktree management page is opened (a `list` request), a `prune` request runs, or about 1 second after the archive strip stops (`workspace` / `session-stop`, via an unref'd timer that never keeps the process alive).
- Only checkouts that are both clean (dirty ones are skipped) and unused (in-use ones are skipped) are removed; the snapshot rules from 6.2 still apply before deleting.
- Why off by default: it preserves the Codex-style "do not delete on session end" behavior; enable it when you want disk reclaimed automatically (or clean manually with `/wt-clean` / prune).

- With `autoPrune: true` (the default), every successful creation prunes the repository's oldest checkouts beyond `autoPruneKeep` in the background; dirty checkouts and anything younger than `pruneGraceMs` are left alone.
- A manual prune (the settings page's *Prune now*, or the `prune` endpoint) runs immediately for one or all repositories and returns the removed entries plus the snapshots it created.
- A pruned detached commit gets a `refs/dsh-codex-style-worktree/<name>` snapshot first (see 6.2), recoverable with `/wt-restore` or `git branch <name> <ref>`; uncommitted changes cannot be recovered.

The browser calls through the authenticated `/api` carrier: `connection.rpc.call('/api', 'dsh-codex-style-worktree/<endpoint>', payload, signal)`; the host registers `/api/dsh-codex-style-worktree/<endpoint>` and asserts `message.method === 'dsh-codex-style-worktree/<endpoint>'`; responses are `{ok:true,value}` or `{ok:false,error:{code,message,details}}`.

| Endpoint | Request | Response value | Error codes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `{ sessionId }` | `{ managed, path?, workspaceRoot?, repoRoot?, mode?, branch?, baseCommit?, createdAt?, dirty? }` | `bad-request` |
| `list` | `{ workspacePath? }` | `{ repos: [{ repoRoot, records: [...] }], snapshots: [...], config }` (settings-page management list; `snapshots` is a **top-level** array, each row carrying `repoRoot`, newest first) | `bad-request` |
| `clean` | `{ sessionId, force?, deleteBranch? }` | `{ removed, path, branchDeleted, snapshots, movedTo? }` (`movedTo` means this session's cwd was moved back to the workspace; when the checkout is gone: `{ removed, path, alreadyGone: true, snapshots }`) | `worktree-dirty`, `worktree-in-use`, `not-managed` |
| `prune` | `{ repoRoot? }` | `{ removed, snapshots }` | `bad-request` |
| `placement` | read `{ workspacePath }`; write `{ workspacePath, mode }` | `{ workspacePath, mode, defaultMode, isGit }` | `bad-request`, `not-git-repository` |
| `settings` | `{action:'get'}` / `{action:'set', patch, revision}` / `{action:'reset'}` | `{ ns, revision, writable, values, defaults, fields: [...] }` | `settings-unavailable`, `conflict`, `

- **There is no `create` and no `cancel`**: creation is triggered only by the first message of a Session (first-turn `agent/pre-step`); the progress card's "Cancel" merely hides the card on the client.
- Projection data never goes through RPC; `status` is only used on demand by the chip popover and the settings page.

- **The cost of force-cleaning**: overriding `worktree-in-use` makes the **other** live session lose its current working directory (its cwd points at a deleted checkout) and throws away any uncommitted changes in it; cleaning your own session's checkout is not refused, its cwd is moved back to the original workspace.
- **Restored checkouts are not managed by the plugin**: they are not written to sidecar records and are not bound to a session, so remove them manually with `git worktree remove`; snapshots only hold the pre-delete committed HEAD.
- **Snapshots only contain committed content**: the ref points at the pre-delete `HEAD`, so uncommitted changes are not in it; a restored checkout is not bound to the original session either.
- **Archive cleanup is a lazy sweep**: `cleanupOnArchive` is not immediate; it only runs at the moments listed in 6.3, and skips checkouts still used by a live session.

Out of scope: cloud / Codex Web integration / multiple placements; automatic merge, PRs, environment installation; remembering placement per session (instead of per workspace); switching an existing session into a worktree mid-conversation.

| Symptom | Action |
| --- | --- |
| No placement selector on the new-session hero row | It only shows for a blank new session whose workspace is a Git repository; existing sessions and non-Git workspaces hide it (check `isGit` from the `placement` RPC). |
| Selected "New local worktree" but nothing was created | Confirm the workspace's placement is still `worktree` when you send the first message (it is remembered per workspace and may have been switched to `local`); look for the first-step skip reason in the session log; confirm `enabled: true`, the repository has a commit, `maxPerRepo` is not reached and there is no disable marker. |

Local development and checks:

```sh
npm test                 # unit / integration tests (node --test)
npm run smoke            # host + client smoke
npm run verify           # the above + node --check client/client.js
npm run install:dry      # direct-install dry run
